title: Frugal living
hook: in caring for people and serving heaven, nothing beats frugality (Tao Te Ching 59)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was fortune and misfortune: each leans on the other, and nobody can call the ending early. Your line was who can tell.

The battery icon turns red, mid-afternoon, a long way from a charger. The phone offers low power mode, and everything changes. The screen dims. The apps stop refreshing in the background. Nothing important stops working, but nothing is wasted either, and the battery lasts into the evening. A new week starts today, and chapter fifty-nine of the Tao Te Ching opens it with a word that can sound dull: frugality. Low power mode, for a whole life. It turns out to be less about pinching pennies than about where strength comes from.
screen: `A RED BATTERY, MID-AFTERNOON.` → `LOW POWER MODE.` → `FRUGALITY, FOR A WHOLE LIFE.`

segments.voice: First, the claim. In James Legge's translation: "For regulating the human (in our constitution) and rendering the (proper) service to the heavenly, there is nothing like moderation." Legge says moderation. Other translators say frugality, or thrift, or sparing. It's one Chinese character, and it carries the sense of not spending more than you need. Notice what it's for: caring for people, and serving heaven. Not getting rich. Second, why it matters. This sparing, the chapter says, lets you turn early, to prepare before you're forced to, and that is called piling up virtue, again and again. Frugality here isn't going without. It's storing up. Every bit not wasted becomes a reserve. Third, what the reserve does. With enough stored, there's nothing that can't be met, and no one can see the limit of it. Someone like that can be trusted with a whole country, and what they hold lasts. Then the closing picture: a deep root and a firm stem, the way of long life and lasting sight. A tree that doesn't spend all its sap on leaves. Fourth, beyond the purse. Frugality can mean money, and it can also mean energy, attention, words. Not answering every message the minute it arrives. Not spending your best hour on the scroll. Not using up your patience by noon on things that didn't need it. In this reading, what you don't waste becomes what you have to give when it counts.
screen: `NOTHING LIKE MODERATION.` · `SPARING IS STORING UP.` · `DEEP ROOT, FIRM STEM.` · `MONEY, ENERGY, ATTENTION, WORDS.` · then, large: `THE WAY OF LONG LIFE AND LASTING SIGHT.`

segments.voice: Let your breath go easy, no bigger than it needs to be, and notice how little effort a breath actually takes. Then look at the day ahead for one small leak, a purchase you don't need, an hour you'd give to the screen, a reply you'd send just to win, and choose one small thing to keep instead of spend. Picture setting it aside like a coin in a jar, and rest with the feeling of a little in reserve.
Frugal living. Chapter fifty-nine: for caring for people and serving heaven, nothing beats moderation. What isn't wasted becomes a reserve, a deep root and a firm stem. Today's word.
Your line: frugal. A deep root keeps something back for the dry days. Day one thousand one hundred twenty-one, done.

howItsDone: Readers of the Tao Te Ching often take chapter fifty-nine as a teaching on sparing use of resources, energy and attention, so that a reserve builds up for caring for others.
